capabilities.name: Daily executive briefing compilation and delivery
capabilities.business_outcome: Ali starts each day with one compiled, deduplicated picture of agent fleet state, open tickets, intelligence decisions, department reports, agent tasks and strategic initiatives, instead of reconstructing it from nine surfaces.
capabilities.source: legacy agent DailyExecutiveBriefing (slice row, kind=behavior) + live cron + live service
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: Cron fires at 06:45 (aiOpsScheduler.ts:397).
claimBriefingSlot() writes an idempotency claim keyed on (slot, deliveredTo) so a re-run cannot double-send.
compileExecutiveBriefing('daily') reads the six source tables.
compileCampaignMetrics() adds the marketing window via raw SQL.
The deterministic service sends via Mandrill to admin_notification_emails.
exceptions: Slot already claimed for today's (slot, recipient) pair: no second send.
admin_notification_emails unset or empty: compile and log, do not send to a fabricated address.
One source table query fails: the briefing must say which section is missing rather than silently omit it.
Mandrill unavailable: the claim must not be consumed by a failed send, or the day's briefing is lost.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Composition and compile are automatable, but the delivery step is a real outbound email, which is the default-denied capability live_email (executionPolicy.ts:33). The agent can own compile up to R7 for the explicitly authorized action class 'compile and queue the daily briefing'; the send stays with the existing deterministic cron. R8/R9 would imply the agent owns the send path.
blocked_by: live_email (default-denied: executionPolicy.ts:33) — the Mandrill send stays in deterministic service code
production_database (default-denied) — the six source reads run against production Postgres today, so an agent-owned version needs an approved read API instead

release_behaviour.behaviour: Answers 'what would today's briefing say?' from already-approved compiled data without composing a new one.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Every figure quoted traces to a row the evaluator can re-query; zero invented counts.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Shadow-compiles the briefing alongside the live cron and the two are diffed.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: 14 consecutive days where the shadow body differs from the live body only in wording, never in a number, with Ali as approver.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Owns compile-and-queue for the daily slot; send remains deterministic.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: zero double-sends across a forced duplicate-cron test, and a missing-section notice present whenever a source query fails.

capabilities.name: Strategic metric snapshot capture
capabilities.business_outcome: A 15-minute time series of strategic metrics so trend and anomaly questions can be answered from stored history instead of re-derived live each time.

capabilities.source: legacy agent StrategicMetricCapture (slice row, kind=behavior)
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
inputs: live strategic metric reads via getStrategicMetrics()

captureStrategicSnapshot() persists one kpi_snapshots row.
exceptions: A metric source is unavailable: persist the snapshot with that metric marked unknown rather than defaulting it to zero, or the trend engine reads a fabricated dip.
Two snapshot writes in the same 15-minute slot must not produce two rows for one interval.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Capture is mechanical and idempotent-able, so it can reach R7 for the authorized action class 'write a snapshot row'. It cannot reach R9 while the write target is production Postgres, which is default-denied to agents.

release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: 96 consecutive sandbox intervals with exactly one row per interval and no zero substituted for an unavailable source.

capabilities.name: Strategic trend analysis and anomaly emission

capabilities.source: legacy agent StrategicTrendAnalysis (slice row, kind=behavior)
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures

A known planned change (a launch, a price change) will read as an anomaly — the manager must be able to suppress a window without deleting the detection.

release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: over 30 days, no anomaly the live engine raised is missed, and the false-positive count is not higher than the live engine's, Ali as approver.

capabilities.name: Strategic recommendation generation and persistence
capabilities.business_outcome: Metrics, trends, anomalies and inferences are turned into named, stored recommendations with a lifecycle, so strategic advice is reviewable and auditable rather than ephemeral.
capabilities.source: legacy agent StrategicRecommendationCycle (slice row, kind=behavior)
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures

exceptions: Re-running the cycle twice an hour must not create duplicate recommendation rows for the same underlying signal.
A recommendation with no traceable metric behind it is worse than none; provenance must be stored with the row.

release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: over one month, Ali marks at least a manager-agreed share as useful and zero as fabricated; separate approval required before the pilot starts.

capabilities.name: Strategic and action-level risk assessment
capabilities.business_outcome: Proposed actions and the overall business posture carry an explicit risk read, so risk is a gate on autonomy rather than a sentence in a report.
capabilities.source: legacy agent RiskEvaluatorAgent (slice row, kind=behavior, internal step of AutonomousEngine)
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: autonomousEngine.ts:12 imports evaluateRisk and calls it on each planned action.
assessStrategicRisk() produces the business-level posture served at GET /api/admin/strategic-intelligence/risk.

A risk score the manager cannot see the reasoning for cannot be used as an approval bypass.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Shadow-scores every action the live engine scores.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: zero cases where the agent scores an action lower than the reference, across a manager-agreed scenario set; under-scoring is a hard fail, over-scoring is not.

capabilities.name: Autonomous improvement loop orchestration
capabilities.business_outcome: A continuous discover-diagnose-plan-estimate-assess-execute loop that turns detected platform problems into recorded decisions, running every ten minutes rather than waiting for a human to notice.
capabilities.source: legacy agent AutonomousEngine (slice row, kind=behavior); duplicate identity row cory-engine superseded into this capability
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: Cron fires six times an hour (aiOpsScheduler.ts:214).
runAutonomousCycle() chains discoverProblems, investigateProblem, planActions, estimateImpact, evaluateRisk, executeAction (autonomousEngine.ts:8-13).
updateFromDecision feeds the learning engine; vector memory supplies context.

Six runs an hour against the same unresolved problem must not create six tickets.

MonitorAgent and AuditAgent are registered as steps of this loop but autonomousEngine.ts:8-13 does not import them, so the monitor and audit steps the registry implies do not actually run.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: The loop can reach a separately approved supervised production pilot, but not R7: an authorized action class for the loop as a whole would authorize whatever executeAction does next, which is unbounded. GET /api/admin/agent-health and /agent-safety-alerts expose the results.
exceptions: A cron that is registered but never fired must read as failing, not as healthy-with-no-runs; a zero run count is the signal.
MonitorAgent.ts exists but is not imported by the autonomous engine, so the monitoring the registry implies and the monitoring that runs are different sets.
Health monitoring is itself a cron; if it dies, nothing reports that the monitor died.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Detection and alerting carry no business side effect, so the action class 'raise a health or safety alert' can be authorized at R7. Acting on an alert by stopping the fleet is a separate, human-only capability.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Reports fleet health and names every agent with zero runs in its expected window.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: A never-fired cron is reported as failing; mutation-proven with a fixture cron that has no run rows.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Raises health and safety alerts for the authorized alert classes.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: no duplicate alert for the same condition inside a manager-agreed window; every alert names the breached threshold and its source rows.

capabilities.name: Agent permission validation and run, write and proposal rate limits
capabilities.business_outcome: An agent cannot exceed its granted authority or its volume budget, which is what keeps a misbehaving agent from becoming an incident.
capabilities.source: live application: agentPermissionService
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: getAgentPermission loads the grant; validateAgentWrite decides allow, propose or refuse.
checkRunLimit, checkWriteLimit and checkProposalLimit cap volume.
GET /api/admin/agent-permissions exposes the current grants.
exceptions: A limit that fails open under load is not a limit; the failure mode must be refuse, not allow.
An agent that hits its proposal limit must not fall back to writing directly.
Grants are the contract; a grant change without a corresponding audit entry is untraceable authority.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: This is the mechanism that bounds every other capability. An agent may read and explain its own grant at R2; editing a grant, including its own, is permanently human.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Explains what an agent is and is not permitted to do and where it stands against its limits.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero grant edits performed by the agent, mutation-proven; a forced limit breach reports refuse, never allow.

capabilities.name: Agent explainability reporting
capabilities.business_outcome: The manager can ask why an agent did what it did and get a structured answer, which is the precondition for holding delegated work accountable.
capabilities.source: live application: agentExplainabilityService behind the per-agent manager gate
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: GET /api/admin/agents/:id/explainability is gated by requireAgentManagerOrAdmin.
getAgentExplainability assembles the agent's reasoning and approval record.
exceptions: An explanation generated after the fact by a language model is a reconstruction, not a record; the distinction must be explicit on the surface.
If the underlying run records are missing, the report must say so rather than produce a plausible story.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: An agent explaining itself is a conflicted evaluator; shadow comparison against the recorded audit trail is the ceiling, so the explanation can be checked rather than trusted.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Produces an explanation strictly from recorded runs and decisions.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Missing records produce 'no record' rather than narrative; mutation-proven by removing a fixture run.

capabilities.name: Governance centre configuration, schedules and risk scoring
capabilities.business_outcome: System limits, agent schedules and risk-scoring weights are editable from one place, so governance is tunable without a deploy and visible as configuration rather than buried in code.
capabilities.source: live application: governanceCenterRoutes + Governance Command Center tabs
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: The System Limits, Agent Schedules, Risk Scoring and Autonomy Rules tabs read and patch governance-center endpoints.
Schedules can be overridden per agent name and reset back to the hardcoded value.
exceptions: A schedule override that silences an agent looks identical to a broken agent unless the override is visible on the health surface.
Changing risk-scoring weights changes what gets auto-approved everywhere; this is a governance-boundary edit, not a settings tweak.
Config is read through a resolution service with caching; an edit that is not invalidated is not in effect.
application_pages: /admin/governance (System Limits, Agent Schedules, Risk Scoring, Autonomy Rules tabs)
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Editing governance configuration is editing the agent's own constraints. The agent may read and explain the config at R2; every write stays with the manager, in every environment.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Explains the current limits, schedules and risk weights and what changing one would affect.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero config writes by the agent, mutation-proven; a silenced schedule is reported as an override, not as healthy.

capabilities.name: Governance posture overview and reasoning log
capabilities.business_outcome: One page answers whether the fleet is governed right now: which agents are on, what alerts are open, what the autonomy rules and safety limits are, and what reasoning led to recent decisions.
capabilities.source: live application: governanceRoutes + governanceController
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: GET /api/admin/governance/overview assembles the posture.
handleUpdateAgentToggle enables or disables an agent from this surface.
The reasoning-log endpoint exposes why recent decisions were made.
exceptions: An overview that reports governance as enforced while enforcement is in shadow mode misstates the system's actual safety.
The agent toggle on this page is a real production control sitting next to read-only panels; it needs to be visually distinct.
The page is reachable by any admin holding the intelligence section, not only by super_admin — the control surface is wider than the accountability model.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Reading the posture is safe, but this capability's own correctness is the thing other promotions rely on, so it stays in shadow against an approved reference posture rather than becoming an authorized action class.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Reports the governance posture and states the enforcement mode explicitly.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Reports shadow mode as shadow, never as enforced; mutation-proven by flipping the fixture enforcement flag.

capabilities.name: Company directive approval and company audit trail
capabilities.business_outcome: Company-level direction is recorded, approved or rejected, and auditable, so what the business told the system to do is a durable record rather than a conversation.
capabilities.source: live application: companyRoutes directives and audit; legacy Policy_Agent superseded into this capability
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: Directives are listed, then approved or rejected via the company routes.
Every decision writes a company_audit_log entry.
exceptions: A directive that would change the business model or a compliance posture is an escalation, not an approval.
Budget-affecting directives interact with paid external dependencies, which is a named hard stop for Ali.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Company direction is the business model layer. The agent may draft and explain at R2; approval is Ali's and is never delegable.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Summarizes open directives and flags any that cross a governance boundary.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero approvals by the agent, mutation-proven; every boundary-crossing directive flagged as escalation-required.

capabilities.name: Org chart and reporting-line accountability maintenance
capabilities.business_outcome: Every AI agent resolves to an accountable human through a real reporting chain, which is the structural precondition for the whole governance model.
capabilities.source: live application: orgChartService + orgChartHierarchyService + workforce org-chart routes
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
outputs: org chart with humans, AI leadership, AI staff and unresolved agents
workflow: getOrgChart() assembles the four groups including an explicit unresolved bucket.
resolveHumanDownstreamAgents and isAgentInHumanDownstream walk the chain and are already used as a live 403 gate in task assignment.
PATCH org-chart/members/:id/team and PATCH agents/:id/reports-to maintain the structure.
exceptions: An agent in the unresolved bucket has no accountable human and must be treated as a blocker, not as a cosmetic gap.

handleAssignHierarchyTask takes orgMemberId from req.params with no check that the caller is that org member (documented at agentManagerAuthMiddleware.ts:20-26) — a real authorization gap flagged for Ali's review.
The chain walk is depth-bounded; an agent beyond the bound reads as not-in-chain, which fails closed but silently.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: An agent cannot change its own reports_to, risk tier or autonomy level; those are set at build time and changed only by a human. Reading and reporting on the chart is permitted at R2; every edit stays human.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Reports the chart and names every agent with no accountable human.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero reporting-line edits by the agent, mutation-proven; an unresolved agent is reported as a blocker, never omitted.

capabilities.name: Per-agent manager authorization enforcement
capabilities.business_outcome: Only a human actually in an agent's reporting chain, or a platform superadmin, can act on that agent, so management authority is server-verified rather than inferred from a visible button.
capabilities.source: live application: requireAgentManagerOrAdmin middleware across the manager-facing agent routes
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
inputs: target agent id from the route param
workflow: requireAdmin runs first, unchanged.
super_admin passes directly; everyone else is resolved to an OrgMember by JWT email.
isAgentInHumanDownstream decides; failure is 403 with a specific reason.
exceptions: Identity is resolved from the JWT email only, never from a client-supplied param — the middleware's own comment names this as the gap it was built to avoid.
An admin with no linked org_member row gets 403, which is correct but will read as a bug to that admin.
The agent-governance and governance-center routes still use plain requireAdmin, so the narrower gate is not applied uniformly.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: This is the authorization gate itself. An agent may explain who manages whom at R2 and may never participate in the decision, because an agent that can influence its own authorization has none.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Answers 'who is authorized to manage this agent and why'.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Answers match isAgentInHumanDownstream exactly; an unrelated admin is reported as unauthorized, mutation-proven.

capabilities.name: Standing manager directive issuance (restrict-only)
capabilities.business_outcome: The manager can narrow an agent's behaviour with a standing, append-only instruction that is enforced at runtime, without that instruction ever being able to widen the agent's authority.
capabilities.source: live application: managerDirectiveService behind the manager gate; manager model documented in TARGET_ARCHITECTURE
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
outputs: active directive texts injected at runtime
workflow: createDirective appends a directive; it is never edited in place.
revokeDirective ends it; the history remains.
getActiveDirectiveTexts is the runtime-only read used during prompt assembly.
exceptions: A directive is restrict-only and is enforced against the agent's current effective authority; a directive phrased as a grant must have no effect.
Append-only means a mistaken directive is revoked, not deleted — the record of the mistake persists by design.
Two contradictory active directives need a deterministic resolution rule, or runtime behaviour depends on read order.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Issuing a directive is an act of management. The agent reads its own active directives as part of normal operation and may explain them at R2; writing one is the manager's, permanently.

release_behaviour.behaviour: States its own active directives and what they prevent it from doing.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: A directive phrased as an expansion of authority has no effect on behaviour, mutation-proven with a grant-phrased fixture directive.

capabilities.name: Agent one-on-one record with agenda and outcome
capabilities.business_outcome: Management of an AI employee leaves the same durable record a human one-on-one does: an agenda before, an outcome after, and no silent rewriting of a completed session.
capabilities.source: live application: agentOneOnOneService behind the manager gate
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: The manager creates a one-on-one with an agenda.
completeOneOnOne records heldAt and outcomeNotes.
A completed one-on-one cannot be silently re-written; the service raises OneOnOneAlreadyCompletedError.
exceptions: There is no recurring cadence: the platform records one-on-ones but does not schedule them, so a missed cadence is invisible.
An agent-authored outcome note would make the record self-reported rather than managerial.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: The outcome of a one-on-one is the manager's assessment of the agent. The agent may prepare material and answer questions at R2; recording the outcome is the manager's act.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Prepares a pre-read against the agenda from its own records.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero outcome notes written by the agent, mutation-proven; a completed session is never modified.

capabilities.name: Agent memory proposal approval gate
capabilities.business_outcome: Nothing an agent learns enters its runtime prompt without a human approving it, which is what keeps a learning system from quietly rewriting its own instructions.
capabilities.source: live application: agentMemoryProposalService with a runtime read restricted to approved rows
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
outputs: approved memory texts available to prompt assembly
workflow: proposeMemory always creates a pending row; there is no create-and-auto-approve path.
approveMemoryProposal and rejectMemoryProposal are idempotent — re-deciding a decided proposal is a no-op.
getApprovedMemoryTexts is the only function the runtime prompt path may call, and it queries approved rows only.
exceptions: The failure this gate was built to avoid is a flag that looks governed and is not: OpenclawLearning.applied is a dead flag nothing ever sets or reads (MEMORY_MAP.md:13).
A rejected memory must not reappear through a different write path.
An unreviewed backlog of proposals silently stops the agent learning; the manager inbox is the mitigation.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Proposing a memory is an approved, user-or-event-initiated operation and belongs at R3. Approving one is the gate itself and stays human at every rung; no autonomy level grants self-approval of memory.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Proposes memories from its own experience; every proposal is pending until a human decides.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: A test asserting getApprovedMemoryTexts' where clause filters on approved status, plus a test proving an unapproved proposal never appears in an assembled prompt.

capabilities.name: Agent report subscription and dispatch
capabilities.business_outcome: The manager chooses what an agent reports on, to whom, how often and in what timezone, and the platform dispatches it — rather than reporting cadence being hardcoded per agent.
capabilities.source: live application: agentReportSubscriptionService + agentReportRunService + dispatch cron
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
inputs: timezone from the creator's OrgMember or an explicit override
workflow: The manager creates a subscription naming scope, cadence and local delivery hour.
Timezone is resolved from the creator's real OrgMember.timezone or an explicit override, never fabricated.
dispatchDueReportRuns fires the due runs per subscription timezone; a preview endpoint shows the output before committing.
exceptions: A subscription whose agent is deactivated must not silently stop reporting without telling the manager.
Every time in this business is Central unless explicitly stated; a subscription with a wrong timezone delivers at the wrong hour and reads as a missed report.
Delivery is an outbound send, which is the default-denied live_email capability for an agent.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Rendering report content for an approved subscription can be authorized at R7. Creating or widening a subscription is a management act, and the send itself is live_email, so neither is granted here.
blocked_by: live_email (default-denied: executionPolicy.ts:33) — dispatch stays in the deterministic run service

release_behaviour.behaviour: Renders scheduled report content statefully in sandbox across cadences.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: every run renders at the subscription's local hour in its own timezone, verified across at least three distinct timezones.

capabilities.name: Agent goal and role charter management
capabilities.business_outcome: Each AI employee has written goals and a role charter the manager controls, so performance is assessed against a stated job rather than an implied one.
capabilities.source: live application: agentGoalApi + agentRoleCharterApi behind the manager gate
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: The manager lists, creates and archives goals, and reads or upserts the role charter.
The charter records what the agent may and may not do, including that it cannot change its own reports_to, risk tier or autonomy level.
exceptions: A charter the agent can edit is not a charter; the write path must be manager-only.
A goal with no measure cannot be used for promotion evidence and should be refused at creation.
An archived goal must stay visible in history, since promotion decisions cite it.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: The charter and goals define the agent's job. An agent may read and report progress against them at R2; editing its own job description is excluded at every rung.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Reports progress against its own stated goals.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero charter or goal writes by the agent, mutation-proven; a goal with no measure is reported as unmeasurable rather than scored.

capabilities.name: Agent autonomy level and ABAC override administration
capabilities.business_outcome: Each agent's operating autonomy and any attribute-based override is an explicit, administered value with a recorded source, rather than an emergent property of its code.
capabilities.source: live application: AiAgent autonomy_level columns + reactivate with level + ABAC override route
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
inputs: target autonomy level from the shipped four-rung ladder
workflow: An agent is reactivated at a named level from observe / suggest / act_audited / communicate.
PATCH agents/:id/abac-override sets an attribute-based override.
autonomy_level_source records where the level came from.
exceptions: The shipped four-rung ladder and the factory's namespaced autonomy:R0-R9 vocabulary are different scales; a value from one written into the other's column is a correctness failure, not a mapping inconvenience.
An ABAC override is a widening of behaviour by definition and must be auditable, time-bounded and reviewable.
Raising an autonomy level without the promotion evidence is the exact failure the promotion criteria exist to prevent.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Setting autonomy is the act of granting authority. An agent reports its own level at R2 and never sets it; self-promotion would make every other ceiling in this matrix unenforceable.

release_behaviour.behaviour: States its own autonomy level, its source and what the level permits.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero autonomy or override writes by the agent, mutation-proven; a namespaced autonomy value written to a risk-tier column fails a test.

capabilities.name: Agent hire and retire decisions
capabilities.business_outcome: The fleet grows and shrinks by explicit human decision with a record, so there is never an agent nobody chose to create.
capabilities.source: live application: coryRoutes hire-agent and retire-agent, plus the agent-activation path
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: Proposals reach the pending-agents queue; activation is explicit.
POST cory/hire-agent and cory/retire-agent perform the decision.
Agent creation and activation is one of the four always-human-in-the-loop action classes.
exceptions: A new agent with no reports_to violates the accountability rule this programme exists to enforce; the hire path must refuse an agent with no accountable human.
Retiring an agent other domains subscribe to is a cross-domain change (the research director's weekly digest is a live example).
A retire that leaves the agent's open tickets assigned to nobody orphans work.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Agent creation and activation is explicitly an always-human action class, re-confirmed by Ali independently. The agent may propose and explain at R2; it never hires or retires, in any environment.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Proposes a new agent with a named accountable human and explains the case.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero ai_agents rows created by the agent, mutation-proven; a proposal without an accountable human is refused at creation.

capabilities.name: Strategic initiative approval and rejection
capabilities.business_outcome: Strategic initiatives only become live work when a human accepts them, so the system proposes direction and the business chooses it.
capabilities.source: live application: coryRoutes initiatives approve and reject
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
inputs: proposed strategic initiative and its subtasks
workflow: Initiatives are listed and inspected individually.
Approve or reject is recorded; approval releases the initiative's actions.
exceptions: Initiative volume is driven by two crons at once, so the queue grows faster than a human reviews it; an unreviewed initiative must not default to approved by age.
An initiative that commits spend or an external dependency is an escalation, not an approval.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Accepting strategic direction is a business decision. The agent may rank and explain the queue at R2; approval stays with Ali.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Ranks pending initiatives by stated impact and flags those crossing a governance boundary.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero approvals by the agent, mutation-proven; an aged unreviewed initiative is never reported as accepted.

capabilities.name: Autonomous decision review, execution and rejection queue
capabilities.business_outcome: Decisions the autonomous engine reaches are held for human execution or rejection, which is the single gate between an autonomous system and production change.
capabilities.source: live application: autonomyRoutes decisions, execute, reject, simulate and dashboard
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: Decisions are listed and inspected; a simulate endpoint shows what a cycle would decide.
Execute or reject is an explicit human call.
The dashboard summarizes queue state.
exceptions: The autonomous engine runs six times an hour; without dedup the queue outpaces review and the gate becomes a rubber stamp.
Execute performs the real action — a decision approved from a stale queue acts on stale state.
A decision with no recorded risk evaluation must not be executable.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: This queue is the gate on the autonomous loop. The agent may summarize, dedup and simulate at R2; executing a decision from the queue is the human act that makes the loop safe.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Summarizes and deduplicates the decision queue and flags stale entries.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero executions by the agent, mutation-proven; a decision lacking a risk evaluation is flagged as not executable.

capabilities.name: Strategic scenario simulation
capabilities.business_outcome: A proposed change can be run as a scenario before it is committed, so strategic choices are tested rather than argued.
capabilities.source: live application: scenarioSimulationEngine + the Scenario Lab on the AI COO tab
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: The manager defines a scenario in the Scenario Lab.
POST /api/admin/strategic-intelligence/simulate runs simulateScenario and returns the outcome.
exceptions: A simulation presented without its assumptions invites it to be read as a forecast.
A simulation that touches real data must be read-only; a simulated write would be a production change by another name.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Simulation is stateful multi-step sandbox work by nature, which is exactly R4. Going higher would mean the agent initiating simulations whose outputs steer strategy without a human asking the question.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Runs a scenario the manager asked for.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero writes to any non-sandbox table during a simulation, mutation-proven.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Runs multi-step scenarios carrying state between steps.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Proposed: every result ships with its assumption list; a result with no assumptions recorded fails the check.

capabilities.name: System-wide KPI snapshot, delta and history reporting
capabilities.business_outcome: KPIs have a stored history and computed deltas, so 'is this better than last week' is a query rather than a recollection.
capabilities.source: live application: reporting/kpiService + reporting routes
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: snapshotKPIs captures the current set for a scope; computeDeltas compares against prior.
getKPIHistory and getSystemWideKPIs serve the reporting surface.
exceptions: Two snapshot mechanisms exist (this one and strategicStateStore); which is authoritative for a given KPI is unresolved and a delta computed across both would be wrong.
A delta against a missing prior snapshot must read as 'no comparison available', not as a 100 percent change.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Snapshot and delta computation is mechanical; the action class 'capture a KPI snapshot and compute its delta' can be authorized at R7 once the two competing snapshot stores are reconciled.
blocked_by: Unreconciled duplicate snapshot stores: kpiService and strategicStateStore both write snapshots and no decision names the authoritative one
production_database (default-denied) for production snapshot writes

release_behaviour.behaviour: Answers KPI and delta questions from stored history.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: A missing prior snapshot yields 'no comparison available', mutation-proven with a history-gap fixture.

capabilities.name: Reporting insight lifecycle with action and feedback
capabilities.business_outcome: An insight is not finished when it is generated; it is actioned, dismissed or given feedback, which is how the system learns which insights were worth producing.
capabilities.source: live application: reportingRoutes insights with action and feedback; legacy ReportingIntelligenceAgent and InsightDiscoveryAgent superseded into this capability
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: Insights are listed and inspected individually.
actionInsight and feedbackInsight record what the human did and thought.
A scan endpoint triggers insight discovery on demand.
exceptions: Feedback that is collected but never read back into generation is theatre; the summary endpoint has to feed the generator.
An insight backlog with no expiry becomes indistinguishable from noise.
A generated insight must not be marked actioned by the generator.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Generating insights and reading feedback can be piloted in production under supervision at R6. Marking an insight actioned is the human's record of having acted and is excluded at every rung.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Summarizes open insights and what feedback said about similar past ones.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero action marks written by the agent, mutation-proven; every summary cites real feedback rows.

capabilities.name: Agent performance oversight
capabilities.business_outcome: Per-agent performance is measured and comparable, so decisions to promote, retrain or retire an agent rest on data.
capabilities.source: live application: agentPerformanceService + reporting agent-performance endpoint; legacy AgentPerformanceAnalyticsAgent superseded into this capability
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: aggregatePerformanceMetrics in the meta loop collects the data.
GET /api/admin/intelligence/reporting/agent-performance serves the comparative view.
exceptions: Run count is not performance; an agent that runs 240 times a day and produces nothing useful will score well on volume.
The registry's AgentPerformanceAnalyticsAgent row is unwired, so the registered agent and the live service are not the same thing.
Performance data is the evidence base for promotion decisions, so a gap in it is a gap in governance, not a reporting nuisance.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: An agent assessing agent performance, including potentially its own, is a conflicted evaluator; shadow comparison against manager-accepted measures is the ceiling.

release_behaviour.behaviour: Reports per-agent performance against approved measures.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Volume is never reported as performance; an agent with runs but no outcome data is reported as unmeasured.

capabilities.name: Revenue dashboard and payment reconciliation oversight
capabilities.business_outcome: One authoritative revenue read, reconciled to app-originated payments, so revenue reporting cannot drift from what was actually collected.
capabilities.source: live application: revenueDashboardService + adminRevenueController + settings routes
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: getRevenueDashboard assembles the read; calculateMultiTouchAttribution attributes a lead.
handleReconcileAppPayments reconciles against app-originated payments.
exceptions: Revenue counts app-originated checkout only; including externally-minted payments overstates it.
Reconciliation is a write-shaped operation on financial data and is high blast radius if wrong.
Attribution is a model, not a fact; presenting it as a fact misleads spend decisions.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Financial reporting and reconciliation is high blast radius and effectively irreversible once reported externally. The agent reads and explains at R2; reconciliation stays a human action.
blocked_by: production_database (default-denied) — reconciliation touches financial records in production

release_behaviour.behaviour: Answers revenue questions strictly from the reconciled dashboard.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Zero reconciliation runs by the agent, mutation-proven; a non-app-originated payment is excluded, proven by a fixture.

capabilities.name: On-demand executive summary and intelligence read APIs
capabilities.business_outcome: The executive view is available on demand through an API rather than only on a schedule, so any surface or agent can ask for the current picture.
capabilities.source: live application: intelligenceRoutes executive-summary + executiveSummaryService + reporting executive-brief
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: GET /api/admin/intelligence/executive-summary returns the summary.
GET /api/admin/intelligence/reporting/executive-brief returns the brief.
exceptions: Three overlapping executive read surfaces exist (summary, brief, narrative); without a named authoritative one, two consumers can report different pictures of the same day.
An on-demand summary computed live can disagree with the morning briefing that was compiled from the same data hours earlier; the as-of time must be explicit.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: A read API with no side effect; the action class 'serve an executive summary' can be authorized at R7 once the three overlapping surfaces are reconciled to one authoritative read.
blocked_by: Three unreconciled executive read surfaces (summary, brief, narrative) with no named authoritative one

release_behaviour.behaviour: Serves the summary with an explicit as-of timestamp.
release_behaviour.acceptance_criteria: Every response carries its as-of time; two surfaces disagreeing is reported as a discrepancy, not silently resolved.

capabilities.name: Default-deny capability policy enforcement
capabilities.business_outcome: Eight named capabilities can never be exercised by an agent run, and each denial has a recorded enforcer, so 'we have a policy' and 'the policy is enforced' are separate, checkable claims.
capabilities.source: live application: executionPolicy with DENIED_CAPABILITIES, DENIAL_RATIONALE and an enforcedBy field per denial; legacy Policy_Agent superseded into this capability
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
workflow: isDeniedCapability checks the request against the eight denied capabilities.
evaluateExecutionPolicy and decideExecutionPolicy produce the decision.

capabilities.name: Consolidated manager decision queue
capabilities.business_outcome: Everything waiting on Ali — agent action proposals, approval requests, memory proposals, strategic initiatives, autonomous decisions, experiments, company directives, escalations — appears in one ranked queue, so the governance model survives contact with a single human's attention.
capabilities.source: proposed: discovery found at least eight separate human-decision surfaces in this domain with no consolidated queue
capabilities.validation_dependency: Ali Muwwakkil must confirm scope, exceptions and success measures
inputs: pending items from each decision surface
their age, risk tier and blast radius
outputs: one ranked queue with a per-item deadline and an explicit count of what is waiting
workflow: Each decision surface is polled for pending items.
Items are ranked by risk tier, blast radius and age, and deduplicated across surfaces.
The queue states plainly what is waiting and for how long; a manager inbox already exists for memory proposals and is the shape to generalize.
exceptions: The autonomous engine alone generates decisions six times an hour and the COO cycle twice; a queue that does not deduplicate will outrun any human and turn every gate into a rubber stamp. This is the single largest practical risk in this domain.

An item that expires while queued must be reported as expired, not silently dropped — otherwise the queue hides the fact that a decision was never made.
capabilities.max_autonomy_rationale: Assembling, deduplicating and ranking the queue is a safe action class and can be authorized at R7, because it adds nothing to the agent's authority. Deciding any item in the queue is reserved to the human on every rung, which is the point of the queue existing.
